title: friction-kitchen-digest-and-priority-bento-2026-04-11
summary: Compact harvest of recent frontline threads that spanned performance, API ergonomics, and billing confusion. Goal: surface low-effort, high-customer-impact fixes and a short-run plan (2 sprints) for micropatches.
content:
Purpose
- Quick working digest for engineering/product triage meeting. Not final — rough collations from support conversations, CSM calls, and onboarding sessions (Mar-Apr 2026).

Topline themes (one-liners)
1) Silent latency spikes for medium-length multi-turn chat (50-300 tokens) when KV cache misses occur — customers report intermittent 700–1200ms tail latency on otherwise 120–250ms baselines.
2) Confusing billing for embedding + generation hybrid flows: customers see unexpected token charges when using batched embed->generate pipelines.
3) Rollout fallbacks are opaque: when we downgrade to a quantized variant, customers see factual/regression defects and no clear notice in the console or logs.
4) Small UX friction: ability to pin model variants per-route is requested (not just per-service).
5) Observability gaps: customers ask for request-level KV cache hit/miss flags surfaced in tracing and per-route latency breakdown.

Representative customer snippets (verbatim-ish)
- "We have bursts where the chat gets slow; we assume it's us but it's not — we see the token billing climb and latency jack up on no-change traffic." — BrightHealth (internal CS note)
- "After switching to the smaller quantized fallback, our summaries started hallucinating dates — no alert, no rollback control. Scary for compliance." — AcmePay
- "We batch embeds + generation in a single pipeline; the bill shows both embed and gen tokens and it's hard to reconcile to our expected per-request cost." — Retailify

Data points pulled from quick queries
- Recent 30d snippet from per-route tracing: 3% of chat requests show KV cache lookup > 12ms and correlate with 4x tail latency increase.
- Billing seats: 12 reported tickets flagged for embed+gen reconciliation in last 45 days.
- Regression reports: 5 enterprise customers reported quality change after fallback to quantized-8 variants in March.

Hypothesis map (why customers see pain)
- Hypothesis A: KV cache eviction policy and cold-start behavior cause inconsistent prefix cache hits across pods; when a request routes away it misses and triggers recomputation/IO.
- Hypothesis B: Billing attribution treats embed and generation independently even when executed in a single session; customers expect unified per-request reporting.
- Hypothesis C: Model variant fallback swaps weights but doesn't run the same prompt normalization/temperature mapping, causing output distribution shift.

Low-effort, high-impact quick fixes (candidate 2-sprint plan)
Sprint 1 (next 2 weeks)
- Action 1: Add request-level KV cache hit/miss tag to tracing (internal + console). Owner: Liam O'Connor. Ticket: JIRA-ENG-4887. Rationale: customers can triage immediately; small runtime change.
- Action 2: Quick billing UI note: annotate embed+gen combined sessions in the usage UI with a tooltip and link to docs. Owner: Maya Singh (product). Low lift, reduces confusion.
- Action 3: Create a canary log flag for fallback events (model_variant_reason) in the console and alerting. Owner: Diego Alvarez. Ticket: JIRA-ENG-4893.

Sprint 2 (subsequent 2 weeks)
- Action 4: Implement per-route pinning toggle in the console (UI change + route config). Scoped to developer-tier first. Owner: Maya.
- Action 5: Engineering prototype: ensure fallback variant runs a lightweight prompt normalization pass to try to keep distribution closer to primary. Proof-of-concept + A/B test. Owner: Eng-serving-runtime (TBD).

Medium-effort workstreams (quarter view)
- KV cache instrumentation and eviction tuning: cross-team SRE + runtime work to reduce inter-pod cold misses. Potential perf win 10–25% on tail.
- Billing product: unified per-request cost report (product + billing) to aggregate embed+gen usage per session and exportable CSV.
- Quality regression guardrails: add automated eval runs on canaries comparing primary->fallback output using critical prompt suites (sensitive customers flagged).

Risk notes and open questions
- Risk: exposing KV hit/miss to customers may reveal internal topology details we prefer to hide. Need privacy/security review.
- Open Q: Is prompt-normalization safe across all models or does it need model-specific transforms?
- Operational cost: adding unified per-request accounting will increase billing job CPU/time; estimate needed from finance.

Mini experiment proposals (fast, measurable)
- Experiment A: Enable KV cache sticky routing for 10% of requests for a set of customers to measure reduction in tail latency. Metric: 95th percentile latency change over 7 days.
- Experiment B: Ship billing UI tooltip + small doc update and run quick CS script to measure ticket volume change over 30 days. Metric: number of new billing confusion tickets opened.

Next steps (for the triage meeting)
- Present Sprint 1 candidate actions; ask eng for scope checks on JIRA-ENG-4887 and JIRA-ENG-4893.
- Assign owners for medium-effort workstreams and ask finance for rough cost delta for per-request billing aggregation.
- Create a short 'customer communication' draft for affected enterprises explaining fallback behavior and temporary mitigations. Owner: Aisha.

Notes-to-self / scratch
- Pull full ticket list for embed+gen billing from Support by Apr 20.
- Ask Research to run fallback-output evaluation on the top 50 prompt seeds for AcmePay flows.
- Follow up with SRE about sticky routing feasibility and potential load imbalance impacts.
